rows.grounds: locative of locus; refers to one's own body as the site of the qualities
abstract quality of being firm or solid as a deity
capacity or worthiness to subdue nāgas and similar beings

items.question: What divine firmness and subjugating powers become established in one's own body?
premises: One's own body serves as the locus for these attainments.
Firmness as a god can be established in that body.
Fitness to subdue nāgas and others arises in that same body.
items.inference: The practitioner's own body becomes the site of divine stability and sovereign subjugating power.
uncertainties: Whether devadṛḍhatā denotes firmness belonging to a deity or firmness in the form of a deity.
items.plain_english: In one's own body arise firmness as a god and the capacity to subdue nāgas and the like.
